# Independent audit: directional comonotone midpoint structure

Source: `candidate 8c097da8eab2cd32`, all four sections. **PASS**, with no global center-selection inference.

## 1. One actual coupling for a direction and both tail orientations

Rotating only the continuous coordinates so that the first coordinate points along `u` is legitimate; no integer-coordinate lattice is changed. The independently audited conditional map remains an actual full-dimensional transport, with the same density ceiling and vector first moment. Its first-coordinate map is increasing quantile transport, so the displayed upper midpoint quantile is exact.

The inverse of a decreasing continuous concave bijection is decreasing and concave; the direction reversal in the written proof is correct. Therefore averaging `Q_A(r^d)` and `Q_B(r^d)`, then taking its inverse, proves the upper-tail root assertion on its support interval. Reversing the same scalar comonotone pair proves the lower-tail assertion for the same coupling. This does not require the remaining triangular coordinates to be unchanged under a second rotation. Endpoints follow from continuity, and the density bound rules out all hyperplane atoms.

The vector mean is independent of `u`, even though the constructed joint measure may change. Thus every one of these directional measures has the same actual middle centroid after combining with `1_K`. The source correctly does not combine measures from different directions in a single integral or pretend to have one direction-independent law with all the new properties.

## 2. Common-tilt mass accounting

For closed endpoint events, neither captured endpoint implies an uncaptured midpoint, and both captured endpoints imply a captured midpoint. Hence `I_A+I_B-I_M` is exactly zero or one. Integrating gives the stated identity with the unused `(1-a/b)U_B` contribution at the same tilt.

On proper cuts, strict monotonicity of the scalar tail gives the quantile-threshold equality. Monotonicity also implies the midpoint probability lies between the endpoint probabilities. The endpoints are nested events in their common quantile parameter, so their intersection and union have the claimed probabilities. At support/full/empty transitions the event identity remains correct even where inversion is no longer an equality of thresholds.

The one-sided centroid consequence follows by Jensen on the concave function `Q_eta(r^d)` under the law `d(r^d)`, whose mean is `d/(d+1)`. The direction of the inequality after applying a decreasing quantile is correct. This proves the constant `Gamma_d` for the directional law without treating that law as uniform on a convex body.

## 3. Complete cone-profile minimization

For cone profiles the support deficits sum to `(w_A+w_B)m^(1/d)` exactly. A full endpoint costs at least the smaller volume `a`. In all other statuses, replacing a negative deficit by zero gives nonnegative `x,y` with `w_A x+w_B y>=c`; sharp Holder gives the stated `C_d m` lower bound. The full-A/empty-B branch is attained at a finite tilt.

When `C_d m<a`, the unconstrained equality allocation has each cost summand below `a`, forcing both normalized deficits below one. It therefore realizes an actual unsaturated pair, rather than an infeasible formal minimizer. At equality the full/empty branch suffices. The `m=0,1` endpoints and the separate linear `d=1` minimization are correctly treated. The homothetic width-ratio check gives `C_d=2v_*` in every dimension, but its saturation branch prevents that coefficient from being used for all tails.

This is an explicit specialization of the archived general two-layer quantile optimization mechanism; its use here retains the actual unused-endpoint term and does not claim a new unrestricted paired-cap theorem.

## 4. Actual failure of the prescribed source

The three listed positive-area fibers are exactly the fibers of their convex hull because the middle and larger endpoint coincide and contain the smaller endpoint. Their midpoint body and homothety coupling are as stated. I independently checked the selected vertical coordinate `166733/500100`, both endpoint thresholds, the middle cap area, and the exact positive target gap `159443/15631250625`.

The finite oblique halfspace therefore refutes the full asymmetric guarantee at that specific source even with genuine midpoint support and both directional tail-root constraints. It does not refute OC or the independently proved nested-endpoint theorem. The source correctly presents this as a limitation of the prescribed center.

Ran `supporting computation verify_directional_comonotone_unused_endpoint_two_sided.py`: **1,740 exact checks passed**. No correction required.

## 5. Appended projected-density concavity theorem

Independently read the new Section 5: **PASS**. I also independently derived its rank-coordinate characterization before reading the source. For `h=f^p`, `q=Q'=1/f(Q)`, and `W=q^(-(p+1))`, the exact local identity is `W'=(p+1)h'(Q)/p`. Positive concave `h` is locally Lipschitz; the quantile and its inverse are locally Lipschitz on compact interior intervals. Thus the almost-everywhere chain rule and preservation of null exceptional sets are legitimate. A monotone representative of `h'` gives concavity of `W`; the converse uses the displayed inverse identity and the same local absolute continuity. No smoothing or second derivative of the original density is assumed.

For quantile interpolation, `W` is the negative-order power mean of the endpoint rank functions. I recalculated its Hessian: the factor and the rank-one positive semidefinite matrix in (17) are correct, including the off-diagonal sign. The mean is increasing in both arguments and concave; composing it with the two concave rank functions therefore preserves concavity. At interpolation weights zero and one it reduces to a coordinate map. The resulting quantile length is finite because its derivative is the corresponding positive convex combination of the two endpoint quantile derivatives.

The convex-body application uses genuine section Brunn--Minkowski with exponent `1/(d-1)` for `d>=2`. The separate `d=1` interval interpretation avoids an undefined exponent. Only the one-dimensional projected density is claimed to have this concavity; neither the full transported density nor one joint measure across all directions is assigned that property. The actual fixed-source failure in Section 4 remains a valid limitation even under this stronger directional constraint.

## 6. Appended all-dimensional fixed-source failure

The new Section 6 also passes independently. The apex coordinate of the selected source is exactly the printed fraction, and subtracting it from one gives the displayed canonical cap volume. The assumptions imply `a<=1/(100d^2)`, so the source has height below one half, the small endpoint is fully captured, and the larger endpoint contributes only its null apex. All three cut statuses are actual and hold uniformly in the stated interval of `epsilon`.

Writing the volume factor as `(1-s)^d` gives the stated twice-integrated quadratic lower bound on its deficit. The successive replacements have the correct signs: the positive linear term uses `(1-epsilon)/(1+2a)>=1-epsilon-2a`, and the negative quadratic term is bounded below by `-d^2 a/2`. The three deductions `d epsilon<=1/10`, `2da<=1/100`, and `d^2 a/2<=1/200` yield `Gamma_d(d+77/200)-1`. At `d=2` this equals `3/50`; for every `d>=3`, `Gamma_d>1/3` makes it strictly larger. Thus the asserted target gap at least `3a/50` is exact and uniform, without an asymptotic remainder. This remains a failure of the prescribed source only.
